To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) WM fibers can be represented and analyzed as strings, (ii) WM fiber clustering is equivalent to string clustering, (iii) a string clustering approach can be used to extract WM fiber-bundles, and (iv) the extracted WM fiber-bundles can be characterized using a model-based technique.

(1) WM fiber-bundles can be extracted and characterized through string-based techniques; (2) WM fibers can be grouped into bundles through a string clustering technique based on string dissimilarity; (3) WM bundles can be characterized by associating them with provided models through a new string-based model characterization technique.
we propose a string-based representation of WM fibers and a string-based clustering algorithm, which allow the extraction of fiber-bundles and the characterization of the WM microstructure.

the following three main tasks: (1) extracting fiber-bundles, (2) characterizing fiber-bundles, and (3) associating fiber-bundles with models.

we propose a new and innovative approach to extracting and representing fiber-bundles, which is based on a new and original string-based formalism and on a novel string-based dissimilarity metric.

we provide an automated approach that can extract and model WM fiber-bundles, possibly different from those present in the initial atlases provided by experts, and, at the same time, can be used to characterize fiber-bundles present in atlases, possibly improving the quality of the models present in atlases.
